cards.explanation: The answer is toward God's holy temple. David says, "I bow down toward Your holy temple…" He sings AND he bows, so his whole self is thanking God. I think that's what happens when thanks gets too big to stay in your mouth. It spills into your knees.

The answer is answered. David says it plain: "On the day I called, You answered me…" Notice he doesn't say God got back to him eventually. He says on the day. David is looking back and giving thanks for exactly that, friends.

The answer is False. David says, "All the kings of the earth will give You thanks, O LORD…" That's every king on earth, not only the ones from home. And he says it will happen when they hear the words of the LORD's mouth, friends.

The answer is hear. David says the kings will give thanks "…when they hear the words of Your mouth." I think that's a good moment for anybody, when somebody tells you good news and you can't stop talking about it.

The answer is because the LORD's glory is great. David gives the reason right in the verse: "They will sing of the ways of the LORD, for the glory of the LORD is great." The kings sing because of who the LORD is. His glory is great, and that's reason enough, friends.

The answer is lowly. David says, "Though the LORD is on high, He attends to the lowly…" High up and still paying attention to the lowly. That's the surprise in the verse, and it's good news for anybody who feels small. I've been small. I've been small in a drawer.

The answer is that the LORD knows them from afar. David says, "but the proud He knows from afar." The lowly get His attention, and the proud get Him from a distance. I'll leave it at what the verse says, friends, and the verse says afar.

The answer is the anger of his foes. David says, "If I walk in the midst of trouble, You preserve me from the anger of my foes…" Notice the "if." He's picturing walking in the midst of trouble, not just around it. I think that's a pretty comforting picture, friends.

The answer is True. David says, "O LORD, Your loving devotion endures forever…" Forever means no expiration date and no best-by stamp. David has just said the LORD will fulfill His purpose for him, so he's ending on solid ground, friends.

The answer is that God not abandon what His hands made. David's last line is, "…do not abandon the works of Your hands." He ends with a request, and it comes right after saying the LORD's loving devotion endures forever. After all that confidence, he still asks. I think that says a lot about how close he feels to God, friends.
